body.statement: Suppose \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\). If the true fixed schedule belongs to \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\), then for every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \(\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\).
body.justification: Pointwise maximization over null-consistent sharp schedules preserves finite-sample design validity.
body.gap: Caughey et al. establish bounded-null validity without network coupling, while Owusu's network heterogeneity procedure is asymptotic.
body.consumer: Applied researchers obtain exact finite-population statements about how many farmers have direct effects above a scientifically chosen threshold.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(Y\) denote the true fixed schedule.  Under the bounded null in the theorem,
for every realized assignment \(x\), the schedule \(Y\) is consistent with the
outcomes observed at \(x\) and satisfies the effect-count restriction.  Hence
\(Y\in\Theta_{r,c}(x,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}(x))\).  Statistic imputability and fixed peer
exposure make the score vector
\[
s_Y(y)=T(y,Y_Y(y)),\qquad y\in\Omega,
\]
a well-defined deterministic vector once the fixed schedule is held fixed.  By the
definition of the supremum,
\[
p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(x)
\geq p_K(x;s_Y)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\Omega.
\]
The subset condition and \(\texttt{thm:universal-validity-iff}\) imply
\[
\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p_K(X;s_Y)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha.
\]
The pointwise inequality reverses the inclusion of lower-tail events:
\[
\{p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha\}
\subseteq\{p_K(X;s_Y)\leq\alpha\}.
\]
Taking design probabilities proves the result.  The fixed-potential-outcome and
outcome-free-kernel assumptions are essential here: they ensure that the same
deterministic score vector and kernel are used at every possible value of \(X\).
